text:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert PD-78921 fired -> eng-sre-oncall. Trigger: prometheus.scrape_failures for job=metrics-ingest-exporter, failing targets > 60% over 2m. Auto-page to devin (oncall).

devin (oncall): acked. looking now. seeing a cascade of scrape timeouts + kafka consumer lag spikes in logs.

maria: +1. is this affecting customer dashboards or just internal monitoring?

devin (oncall): customer-facing dashboards are delayed. grafana shows a missing-series burst for multiple orgs (some customers report missing alerts). I count ~180k log messages queued in log-ingest-kafka.

alex: logs from exporter: "ERROR: scrape timeout after 10s" repeatedly. exporting node metrics not responding. looks like CPU throttling on the exporter pods.

devin (oncall): running quick commands: 
```
kubectl -n metrics get pods -l app=metrics-exporter -o wide
kubectl -n metrics logs deploy/metrics-exporter --since=10m
kubectl -n ingest get sts -l app=kafka-consumer
```

jordan: kafka consumer lag metric: consumer_group=log-ingest-consumers lag=2.4M, processing rate dropped from 55k/s to 7k/s since 02:12 UTC.

maria: probable root cause hypothesis: exporter process is getting CPU throttled -> scrape timeouts -> backlog => consumers overwhelmed -> increased lag -> alerts. Could be a noisy job or autoscaler misfire.

devin (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) scale metrics-exporter replicas to 6 temporarily; 2) bump resources for exporter pods (cpu request/limits); 3) pause non-critical heavy scrapes (we have a list in runbook); 4) scale consumers to drain kafka backlog. Doing step 1 now.

alex: i'll prepare a small patch to increase cpu request from 200m->500m, limit 1000m. Also applying a horizontal pod autoscaler change to lower threshold.

incidentbot: PD-78921 -> acknowledged by devin (oncall). PagerDuty note: assigned to eng-sre.

devin (oncall): scaled exporter to 6 replicas (kubectl scale deployment/metrics-exporter --replicas=6). CPU spikes dropped immediately, but some pods still in CrashLoopBackOff on one node. Investigating node-level pressure.

jordan: node metrics show node-7 has 98% iowait and kernel softirq high. That node hosts 3 exporter pods + 2 kafka brokers. Suggest cordon + drain node-7 if it's the hotspot.

maria: agreed. cordon and migrate workloads off node-7, restart kubelet if needed. That should let exporters stabilize. Also let's temporarily reduce scrape_interval for heavy targets from 15s->60s (runbook section 4) to reduce load.

devin (oncall): cordoned node-7 and started drain. restart kubelet scheduled if pods don't come up. applying scrape-interval override for heavy targets (metrics-heavy tag) now.

alex: resource patch applied to metrics-exporter, new pods coming up with increased cpu. also turned on fallback exporter (lightweight) for 10 heavy targets to reduce load.

jordan: after scaling consumers to 8 replicas, consumer throughput jumped to ~48k/s, lag decreasing. kafka backlog now ~320k and counting down.

devin (oncall): customer impact: 5 customers reported delayed dashboards/alerts for ~22 minutes. notified customer-ops and posted to #support. creating INC ticket INC-2026-123 to track. marking severity: P2 for now (partial degradation).

maria: good. can we enable smart routing so critical customers get prioritized ingestion while backlog drains? check routing policies.

alex: enabled temp routing policy that prioritizes orgs with SLA tag "enterprise". we should see critical orgs catch up faster.

devin (oncall): monitoring: scrape failure rate falling from 65% -> 8% over last 6m. consumer lag trending down. keeping pages open until all backlogs < 10k and exporters stable.

incidentbot: PagerDuty note: escalated to senior-oncall after 20m of ack.

maria: action items for post-incident: 1) investigate cause of node-7 iowait (disk/network), 2) validate HPA for exporters under burst load, 3) add a slow-scrape circuit breaker to avoid cascade, 4) run a chaos test for exporter overload. assign owners?

devin (oncall): i'll own immediate node postmortem and temp playbook updates. alex owns HPA + resource defaults. jordan owns consumer scaling playbook and routing policy tests. maria to coordinate customer comms and incidence timeline.

lee: i'm taking second-shift handoff in 20 minutes. can you summarize status and next steps I need to watch for?

devin (oncall): summary for handoff -> current status: exporters stable, scrape failures down to single digits, kafka backlog 78k and decreasing, critical orgs prioritized. open actions: drain node-7 remediation follow-up, revert temp scrape-interval changes after stabilization, monitor consumer lag until <10k, validate no remaining CrashLoopBackOffs. INC-2026-123 tracking notes.

maria: adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/metrics-scrape-failure. Please annotate with timestamps and commands used.

lee: got it. i'll monitor consumer lag and keep PagerDuty escalation policy engaged if lag stops decreasing. if anything regresses i'll page devin. thanks team. :thumbsup:

devin (oncall): handing off to lee in 10m. leaving a small checklist in the ticket. good work everyone.

jordan: nice work. I'll follow up with a short postmortem draft after node analysis.

incidentbot: Thread closed by devin (oncall) - follow-up notes moved to INC-2026-123.
